ZTS.thesis_one_line: The world's top animal-health company, priced cheaply after two guidance cuts and a securities lawsuit over slowing US pet-medicine demand.
kill_criteria: U.S. companion-animal organic revenue declines for a 3rd consecutive quarter (Q3'26 report, due ~Nov 2026).
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut a third time at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release.
Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 2.5x (vs ~1.6x now) without a specific offsetting M&A rationale.
The securities class action survives a motion to dismiss and/or the SEC opens a formal (not preliminary) investigation.
Livestock organic growth (currently the offset) decelerates below +5% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 guidance cut twice in six months: revenue $9.825-10.025bn -> $9.68-9.96bn -> $9.12-9.32bn; adj. EPS $7.00-7.10 -> $6.85-7.00 -> $6.15-6.25; organic growth flipped from +3-5% to -3% to -1%.
U.S. companion animal product sales -11% YoY in Q2'26; U.S. canine OA pain (Librela/Lenivia) revenue -24% YoY to $34mm.

Federal securities-fraud class action filed 2026 (S.D.N.Y., City of Ann Arbor Retiree Health Care Benefit Plan & Trust v. Zoetis Inc., No. 26-cv-04401) alleging misstatements re: Librela adoption, Simparica Trio and Apoquel/Cytopoint share loss; related shareholder derivative suits filed June 2026.

Consolidated long-term debt rose from $5,231mm (2025-06-30) to $9,042mm (2025-12-31), largely funding $3,235mm of FY2025 buybacks (incl. a $1,535mm accelerated buyback Dec 2025) plus $1,190mm more in H1'26, even as growth decelerated.
data_conflicts: b1 composite score (0.51, decile 6/10) still rates ZTS mid-pack on stale filed fundamentals (last_filed_date 2026-08-06) that understate how large the Q2'26 guidance cut was; diligence overrides the quant score here.

Prior triage (Q08) framed the issue as temporary Librela/Solensia channel destocking; primary-source evidence (Q2'26 release, class action) shows a broader U.S. companion-animal demand problem across multiple franchises (Simparica Trio, Apoquel/Cytopoint), not just Librela channel dynamics.
ZTS.confidence_in_thesis: medium (valuation cheap and moat intact, but two consecutive guidance cuts and active securities litigation mean one more quarter of evidence is needed before sizing up)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ZTS yet, so there is nothing to reconcile; our own reverse DCF (required return ~7.5% vs FCF yield 6.87%) implies only ~0.6%/yr perpetual growth, below our base case of ~3%/yr, i.e. the market has already priced in most of the bad news.

ZTS.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 adj. EPS ~$6.20 (post-cut guidance midpoint), 10y earnings growth bear -2%/base +3%/bull +7% per year, exit NTM P/E bear 10x/base 12.5x/bull 15x (vs 11.0x now), plus ~2.5-3% dividend yield each year.

AEE.thesis_one_line: Missouri-Illinois regulated utility with a large grid-and-data-center capex program and solid guidance, but on the programme's dividend model the price already asks for about 8% a year of dividend growth against a 5-5.75% base case.
kill_criteria: Full-year 2026 diluted EPS comes in below $5.25 (the low end of guidance) at the Q4'26 report.
The pending Missouri rate case ($343mm requested) is settled/ordered at less than 60% of the requested revenue increase.
Consolidated debt/(debt+equity) rises above 65% (vs ~60% now) without a matching equity raise already announced.
Rate-base CAGR guidance (currently 10.6%, 2025-2030) is cut at any quarterly update.
Two consecutive quarters of EPS growth below 3% YoY.
key_adverse_facts: [DV02 2026-10-06, replaces the original] FY2026 guidance $5.25-5.45 is on the adjusted basis: FY2025 adjusted EPS was $5.03 (GAAP $5.35 includes $0.32 of tax benefits), so the guide implies +4% to +8%, not zero growth. The reservation is valuation: price implies about 7.9%/yr dividend growth (10 years, 3% terminal, cost of equity 7.6%) against a 5-5.75% base.
Structurally negative free cash flow by design (H1'26 OCF $1,191mm vs capex $2,653mm = FCF approx -$1,462mm); Ameren is a continuous capital-markets issuer, so financing-cost risk is unhedged.
Missouri filed a $343mm rate increase request in 2026, not yet decided -- regulatory outcome risk against an aggressive capex plan.

H1'26 EPS strength (+19.6% Q1 YoY, +11.9% Q2 YoY) was not flowed into a guidance raise, suggesting it may include weather/timing benefits rather than pure algorithm delivery; we could not obtain an explicit company reconciliation this cycle.
data_conflicts: None identified between b1/d4 quant data and filings; b1 rates AEE top-quintile (decile 9/10) on quality and low volatility, consistent with the regulated-utility profile confirmed in filings.
AEE.confidence_in_thesis: medium (regulated model and capex visibility strong; DV02 valuation recompute shows no margin of safety at $99.39: base-case IRR about 6.7-6.9% vs 7.6% cost of equity)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV02 2026-10-06: original one-stage Gordon (r 7.7%, implied perpetual 4.8%) compared a perpetual rate with a ten-year base rate. Programme dividend model (10 years constant growth, 3.0% terminal, cost of equity 5.17% + Blume beta 0.58 x ERP 4.14% = 7.6%, price $99.39, dividend $3.00) implies 7.9%/yr 10-year dividend growth (6.4% at 7.1%, 9.3% at 8.1%) vs base 5% (or guided 6-8% fading to 4.5% = 5.75%): dividend-model value $79-85, price 17-26% above. No V1 row for AEE. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH under the rule that INCLUDE-SMALL requires implied at or below base.

AEE.scenario_basis: Starting NTM EPS ~$5.72, 10y earnings growth bear +2%/base +5%/bull +7.5% per year, exit NTM P/E bear 15x/base 17x/bull 19x (vs 17.4x now), plus ~2.9% dividend yield each year.

ALLE.thesis_one_line: Leading door-lock and electronic-access-control maker with a strengthening balance sheet and a raised 2026 outlook, but priced about in line with its base-case growth after correcting the valuation.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance (currently $8.85-9.00) is cut at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release.
Consolidated operating margin falls below 19% for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x (vs ~1.6x now) without a stated, offsetting M&A growth rationale.
Americas electronics revenue growth decelerates below high-single-digit YoY for two consecutive quarters.
International segment organic revenue is negative for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: Q1'26 operating margin dipped to 18.9% (vs 20.9-22.2% in adjacent quarters) alongside a reported EPS miss that the market reacted negatively to.
Management describes the international segment as 'weaker' even in the same quarter it raised full-year guidance; the drag is real but unquantified in sources reviewed this cycle.

[DVH1 2026-10-06] replaces the original: FY2025 capex was $98.1M and available cash flow $685.7M (106% of net earnings), so the data gap is closed; H1 2026 available cash flow was $260.8M vs $275.4M (receivables timing).
data_conflicts: None identified between b1/d4 quant data and filings; b1's weak momentum percentile (21st) sits against improving fundamentals (guidance raised twice, equity up ~57% since 2023), consistent with our INCLUDE call that the market has not yet re-rated the improvement.
ALLE.confidence_in_thesis: medium (FY2025 capex and FCF now confirmed: available cash flow $685.7M; adjusted EPS guide raised once, revenue guide twice; valuation in line with base after DVH1 recompute; international softness unquantified)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: [DVH1 2026-10-06] original Gordon on a 3.69% FCF yield (Yahoo FCF $484M) with an unsupported 8.0% rate implied 4.3% perpetual growth. Programme ten-year model (rf 5.17%, ERP 4.14%, Blume beta 0.89, WACC about 8.4%, 3% terminal; TTM FCF after SBC $641M; EV $14.85bn) implies 5.4%/yr (6.6% at cost of equity) vs 6% base: in line. INCLUDE -> INCLUDE-SMALL. No V1 row exists.

ALLE.scenario_basis: Starting NTM EPS ~$9.56, 10y earnings growth bear +2%/base +6%/bull +10% per year, exit NTM P/E bear 13x/base 16x/bull 18.5x (vs 16.2x now), plus ~1.4% dividend yield each year.
